sources.citation: Dotawo 7 (2021) Comparative Northern East Sudanic Linguistics (Starostin; Blench; Jakobi) and Mother Tongue XIV (2009).
sources.note: Birgid forms from Thelwall 1977 in comparative tables only; 'nearly extinct Birgid.. poor documentation'; no stress.

sources.citation: Sabbar, Sabbar & Herman Bell. 2017. [Nubian toponyms article], Dotawo: A Journal of Nubian Studies 4 (Place Names and Place Naming in Nubia).
sources.note: Only 'The Murgandé (Birgid) Nubian language of South Darfur is now on the verge of extinction'; footnote 7 'The Nubian languages are tone languages. The acute accent here represents a high tone' is a general remark about Nubian, not Birgid-specific.

sources.citation: Blažek, Václav. 1996. [Nubian etymologies] in P. Zemánek (ed.), Studies in Near Eastern Languages and Literatures: Memorial Volume of Karel Petráček. Prague: Oriental Institute.
sources.note: Birgid forms (kwarti 'bird', mel 'dog', kurti-nur 'knee', etc.) cited from Thelwall/MacMichael without accent marks; the volume's stress passages concern Kunama, Gurage and PIE, not Birgid.

sources.citation: MacMichael, H. A. 1918. Nubian elements in Darfur. Sudan Notes and Records 1: 33-53 (Birqed wordlist).
sources.note: Ethnographic account plus comparative Birqed/Midob/Nile Nubian vocabulary; no remark on accent or stress (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/emphasis/tone yields nothing linguistic).

sources.citation: Alamin, Suzan. 2014. Noun Phrase Constructions in Nubian Languages: A Comparative Study. Dotawo: A Journal of Nubian Studies 1.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States: 'Birgid is considered to be a nearly extinct language and is poorly documented. In fact, the only published studies are MacMichael's and Thelwall's Birgid vocabulary of 1918 and 1977, respectively.'

sources.citation: MacMichael, H. A. 1922. A History of the Arabs in the Sudan, vol. 1 (ch. IX Birked, comparative vocabulary). Cambridge: CUP.
sources.note: Birked ethnography and wordlist; nothing on stress.
Descriptive refs: Ushari 1974 (phonology, 45 pp), Zyhlarz 1928 (wordlist, 17 pp), MacMichael 1922 and 1918 (wordlists). Bell 2006 and Thelwall 1977 are absent from Glottolog's list.

sources.citation: Edenmyr, Niklas et al. 2011. [Birgid field report; full title not recovered — cited as 'Edenmyr et al. 2011' by Sands 2017: 14 for two elders recalling about 100 Birgid words].
